source_derived_cases: Exact asymmetric FPBI grid and unnormalized focus direction; maximize/minimize orientation
Batched geometry, flat axes, coincident extrema, duplicate rays and rank-deficient cross-product fallback
Dominated and duplicate extreme filtering before normalization
Actual constrained scalar solves, float32/float64 quadratic front and analytic kappa=0.5
Two-sided decision constraints on extrema and rays; analytic constrained kappa=0.3
Concave front requiring unrestricted negative kappa=1-sqrt(2)
Equality constraints and a real BoTorch GenericDeterministicModel
Explicit selection of a posterior model batch
Failed extreme raises; failed rays remain diagnosed and are omitted
Independently checked infeasibility overrides an injected successful optimizer flag
Nonfinite objectives/constraints, changing output dimension, invalid options and numeric overflow guards
resolved_static_issues: Added explicit NumPy NDArray annotations for ray_ok and the ray start vector; no algorithm change
limits: The optimizer and geometry execute on CPU; CUDA callbacks and returned tensors preserve device but this is not a GPU-native SLSQP implementation.
The dedicated CUDA test is a small two-objective float64 boundary check, not a CUDA coverage or performance study.
Local convergence does not prove globally optimal extrema, globally Pareto outcomes or good front coverage.
The original small FPBI/NSGA-II comparison favored NSGA-II on its four cases and retained unequal actual output cardinalities under a common cap; no performance superiority is claimed.
Failure injection tests are expected rejection paths, not unresolved failures in the final test run.
